transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, I guess what brings me in is that my sleep has just gotten really messed up lately. I'm either staying up half the night because my mind just won't stop running, or I'll fall asleep and then wake up way too early, and I just feel like I haven't rested at all. It's really starting to affect me.
Over the past week or two, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling sad, down, or depressed, or have you noticed any unusual changes in how you're feeling emotionally?

Yeah, it's been pretty bad, honestly. Um, lately I just wake up with this heavy, empty feeling. It's like... even just sitting in my own condo that I worked so hard for just makes me want to cry. So, yeah, I've definitely been feeling sad and down most days.

Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, confident, or 'up' — maybe needing very little sleep but still feeling great, or having racing thoughts and lots of ideas? If so, how long did those periods last?

Yeah, I do get like that. Actually, just earlier in the month I had a few days where I felt almost... lit up and unstoppable. I had all this energy and my mind was just going. 

But it also made me really edgy. I’d snap at my mom, or even my supervisor at work over little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me at all. When that happens, it usually lasts for maybe three or four days before it goes away.

Besides the few days earlier this month when you felt energetic and edgy, have you had other periods like that in the past — times when you felt unusually up, energetic, or irritable for several days at a time?

Um, well, maybe a little bit in the past, but... the really obvious cycling between that charged-up stretch and this heavy crash I'm in now, that's really just been going on for about a month. It started right around the time the mortgage became real.

Before this past month, have you ever had other times in your life — maybe years ago — when you experienced similar periods of feeling really down and depressed, or times when you felt unusually energetic and irritable like you described?

Um, well, as far as feeling down goes... this depressed, guilty fog I'm in has actually been hanging around for about five months now. It just got much worse recently after I bought the condo. So yeah, that part has definitely been going on for a bit longer than just this past month.

Going back further in your life — say, before this past year — have you ever had periods lasting a week or more where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep, or had racing thoughts, even if you didn't feel irritable?

No, I don't think so. I mean, not that I can remember. Before this year, I think I was pretty much just... normal. I never had anything where I felt super energetic or didn't need sleep for a week or anything like that. It's really just been this recent stuff.

You mentioned feeling depressed for about five months now. Before those five months started — let's say last year or earlier — would you say your mood was pretty normal and stable for an extended period of time?

Yeah, before this started about five months ago, my mood was fine. I just went to work, did my bookkeeping, and lived my life. I didn't have any of these heavy, down periods or the edgy, energetic stuff before this year. Everything was pretty stable and normal for as long as I can remember.

When you felt that charged-up energy earlier this month that lasted three or four days — during that time, did you notice you needed significantly less sleep than usual, like maybe only a few hours a night, but still felt rested and energetic?

Yeah, actually. Um... during those few days, there were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours. But the weird thing was, I didn't feel tired at all. I would just get up feeling completely charged, like I didn't even need my morning coffee to get going.

You said that charged-up period lasted three or four days — I want to make sure I have this right. Did that energetic, irritable feeling actually last for the full four days, or was it closer to just two or three days?

Honestly, I'm not entirely sure. I didn't really mark it down on a calendar or anything, so it kind of just... blurs together a bit. It was probably closer to three days, maybe four? I just know it was a few days in a row where I felt completely wired like that before it stopped.

Let me ask you this more carefully: During that period earlier this month when you felt wired and energetic and needed only a few hours of sleep — on how many consecutive days did that feeling actually continue without stopping?

I really can't say for sure. Like I said, I didn't write it down. It was just a few days in a row where I felt like that, but I couldn't tell you exactly how many consecutive days it was. It's just hard to remember the exact number.
I understand it's hard to remember exactly. But thinking back to that wired, energetic period — do you think it lasted at least four days in a row, or was it probably shorter than that?

I really don't know if it was four days. It might have been, or it might have just been three. I just know it was a few days where I felt like that, but I can't say for sure if it hit the four-day mark.

I know you're not certain about the exact number of days, but let me ask it this way: During that wired, energetic period earlier this month, did you feel that way for at least 4 full days in a row, or do you think it was less than 4 days?

I know you're trying to get a firm answer on this, but I really just don't know. Like I've been saying, it could have been less than four days, or it could have been four. I just didn't pay that close attention to the exact timing while it was happening. It was just a few days in a row of being really revved up, and that's... that's really all I can remember about how long it lasted. I'm sorry, I just can't give you a definite yes or no.

During those few days earlier this month when you felt wired and energetic, did anyone else — like your mom or supervisor — comment on how different you were acting, or did anything happen at work or home that stands out as unusual for you?

Well, my mom definitely noticed. During those days, I just felt... I don't know, almost lit up, like I was unstoppable. But then I'd turn around and just snap at her over nothing. Like, really little questions that normally wouldn't bother me at all. And it happened at work, too. I snapped at my supervisor. It was just... I felt so charged up, but also really irritable at the same time. So yeah, people definitely noticed I was acting different.
During those few days when you felt wired and energetic, were you able to do your job normally, or did your work suffer in some way because of how you were feeling and acting?

Well, I'm still getting to work, but it hasn't been great. I've made enough reconciliation mistakes that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to talk about it. So yeah, my work has definitely suffered a bit. And outside of work, I've just been avoiding my salsa class and my friends because I just don't feel like myself right now.

You mentioned feeling depressed for about five months now, and then earlier this month you had those few days where you felt wired and energetic. Between the time the depression started five months ago and those energetic days earlier this month, was there a clear period in the middle where your mood felt more normal — or has the depression been pretty much continuous the whole time?

It's been pretty much continuous. That depressed, guilty fog has been hanging around for about five months now. I mean, it definitely got a lot worse after I bought my condo, but it hasn't really let up or gone back to normal since it started.

Besides that wired, energetic period earlier this month, have you ever had another time in your life — maybe years ago — when you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, and felt that way consistently for a full week or longer?
No, I don't think so. I can't really remember any time where I felt like that for a whole week. It was just those few days recently. Before that, I don't recall anything similar happening.

Between the time the depression started five months ago and those energetic days earlier this month, was there a clear period in the middle where your mood felt more normal — or has the depression been pretty much continuous the whole time?

patient.answer: It's been pretty much continuous. That depressed, guilty fog has been hanging around for about five months now. I mean, it definitely got a lot worse after I bought my condo, but it hasn't really let up or gone back to normal since it started.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has experienced hypomanic or manic episodes meeting duration criteria (≥4 consecutive days for hypomania, ≥7 for mania) to differentiate F31.9 (Bipolar II or I) from F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder). The patient's recall of the recent energetic period is vague (3-4 days, uncertain), so I need to establish if there's any other past episode that was clearly longer and better-defined.
doctor.question: Besides that wired, energetic period earlier this month, have you ever had another time in your life — maybe years ago — when you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, and felt that way consistently for a full week or longer?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have ever had a full manic episode lasting a week or longer in the past, which is not covered by my current symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't think so. I can't really remember any time where I felt like that for a whole week. It was just those few days recently. Before that, I don't recall anything similar happening.

inference.note: Ruled out F31.9 (Bipolar Disorder). The patient's energetic period lasted only 3-4 days (likely <4 days), which is insufficient for a hypomanic or manic episode (requiring ≥4 consecutive days for hypomania, ≥7 for mania). No prior history of mood elevation episodes. The 5-month depressive episode with recent worsening, irritability during the brief energetic period, and functional impairment are consistent with Major Depressive Disorder with possible anxiety features, not bipolar disorder.

Diagnosis is Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, unspecified severity.
